Your systems stay. We connect them.

We work with the software you already run, connect it through supported APIs, webhooks, or exports, and make the results measurable.

What we integrate with

Examples of systems commonly found in logistics. Naming a product does not imply a partnership; integrations depend on the APIs and exports your plan provides.

  • Transport and courier management (TMS)

    System of record for bookings, AWBs or LRs, trips, milestones and delivery outcomes. We read through APIs, webhooks or scheduled exports and write back only agreed instructions or status fields, such as re-attempt choices.

    • Shipsy
    • LogiNext
    • In-house courier or last-mile platforms
    • LR booking and trip management systems
    • Rider and driver apps

  • Warehouse management (WMS)

    Holds item masters, ASNs, receipts, inventory, orders and value-added activity for each client. We read events and snapshots for alerts, statements and billing, and never post inventory adjustments without the warehouse manager.

    • Unicommerce
    • Increff
    • Vinculum
    • SAP EWM
    • Manhattan Active Warehouse Management

  • Freight forwarding and customs

    Hold bookings, house and master bills, documents and customs declarations. Automations read status and documents to build checklists and updates; filing and signing stay with the licensed customs broker.

    • CargoWise
    • Magaya
    • ICEGATE and e-Sanchit
    • Customs broker filing software
    • PCS1x port community system
    • Shipping line and airline portals

  • GPS, telematics and vehicle records

    Provide location, odometer, toll crossings and vehicle and driver records. We use them for ETAs, maintenance and document checks, with access limited to operational purposes.

    • Fleetx
    • LocoNav
    • WheelsEye
    • FASTag statements
    • VAHAN and SARATHI via ULIP

  • GST and transport portals

    Generate and hold statutory documents. Workflows read e-way bill and invoice status and alert people; authorized users generate, extend, cancel and file.

    • E-way bill system via GSP or ERP
    • E-invoice IRP via ERP or GSP
    • DigiLocker
    • mParivahan

  • Messaging and customer channels

    Carry bookings, updates, NDR choices and support conversations. Templates, consent records and opt-outs are managed so shipment updates never carry promotions.

    • WhatsApp Business Platform
    • SMS gateway with DLT-registered templates
    • Masked calling such as Exotel or Knowlarity
    • Helpdesk such as Freshdesk or Zoho Desk
    • Client and merchant portals

  • Accounting and payments

    Hold invoices, receivables, remittances and expense postings. Automations prepare drafts and reconciliations; finance approves postings and payments.

    • TallyPrime
    • SAP Business One
    • Zoho Books
    • Payment gateway and UPI settlement reports
    • Fuel card statements

The measures we propose to track

We agree the definition, population, period, source, and owner of each measure before launch.

On-time delivery against promise
Share of shipments delivered by the date and time promised to the customer or set in the SLA, by lane, service, hub and carrier.Why it matters: The measure customers judge you on; the breakdown shows whether planning, line haul or the last mile is failing.
First-attempt delivery rate
Share of shipments out for delivery that are delivered on the first attempt, excluding reschedules the consignee requested in advance.Why it matters: Every failed attempt costs a trip, delays COD cash and raises the chance of a return to origin.
Return-to-origin rate
Share of shipments in a period returned to the merchant after failed attempts or refusal, by merchant, pin code and reason.Why it matters: Returns cost both the merchant and the network; reason-coded data separates fixable causes from genuine refusals.
Exception resolution time
Median time from an exception being raised, such as a delay, no-movement or failed attempt, to its recorded resolution, by exception type and owner.Why it matters: Shows whether the control tower acts quickly and where ownership or escalation is weak.
POD-to-invoice time
Median days from delivery to a complete POD on file, and from POD to invoice sent, by customer and branch.Why it matters: Billing that waits for paper stretches receivables; the split shows whether POD collection or billing review is the bottleneck.
COD reconciliation lag
Median days from a COD delivery to the collection being matched to a deposit and included in a merchant remittance, with unreconciled value by aging.Why it matters: Merchants judge couriers on remittance speed and accuracy, and unmatched cash is a control risk.
Dock-to-stock time
Median hours from a vehicle reporting at the dock to received goods being available for picking in the WMS, by client.Why it matters: Clients cannot sell stock still sitting on the dock; delays here lead to stock-outs and disputes.
Quote turnaround time
Median business hours from a complete rate request to an approved quote being sent, by mode, lane and customer tier.Why it matters: Shippers often book with the first complete, valid quote; this shows whether pricing capacity or approvals slow you down.
Clearance time
Median time from Bill of Entry or shipping bill filing to out of charge or let export order, with waiting time attributed to queries and missing documents.Why it matters: Points at document quality and query handling, which drive demurrage, detention and customer satisfaction.
Document and permit lapses
Count of vehicles, drivers or riders with an expired license, registration, insurance, PUC, fitness certificate or permit during the period, plus e-way bills expired in transit.Why it matters: Each lapse is a legal, insurance and service risk; the aim is to see them coming, not to count them afterwards.

How we connect systems responsibly

  • Client-owned accounts, data and credentials; we work through agreed roles and permissions.
  • Integrations use official APIs, webhooks or exports where the system provides them; nothing scrapes private portals.
  • Every automation has a named owner, an exception queue and a manual fallback.
  • Messages, prompts and templates are reviewed and approved by the client before launch.
  • AI outputs are grounded in approved sources and checked against an agreed evaluation set before release.
